title: polyglot-sdks: add fail-fast circuit retry profiles and explicit stream abort APIs
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers building high-throughput agents asked for clearer failure behaviour when downstream model capacity degrades, and for an ergonomic way to cancel long-lived streaming responses from application code. This PR introduces two coordinated, backwards-compatible features across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs: 1) a set of "fail-fast" circuit-style retry profiles (small, deterministic retry counts with early circuit open heuristics) that are safe for low-latency interactive workloads; 2) an explicit stream.abort/close API surface that signals the SDK to abort in-flight streams and emit a concise error shape for downstream apps to handle. The goal is parity across SDKs with minimal API churn and a single documented guidance doc for product teams.
commits: feat(sdk-common): introduce RetryProfile type and FailFast presets
feat(py): add StreamHandle.abort() and failfast retry presets; bump to 2.5.0
feat(ts): export AbortableStream and apply failfast defaults; bump to 1.9.0
feat(go): add AbortStream(ctx) convenience and FailFastRetryPolicy; bump to 1.7.2
test: add cross-sdk integration harness for abort + retry interplay
docs: add SDK guidance + migration notes
ci: tighten linting rules for ts and py; adjust go vet expectations
review_comments: Priya Nair: Nice work. Please clarify which retry profile is the default for the hosted API consumer and add guidance for when customers should prefer FailFast vs Conservative.
Maya Chen (author): Added a short decision table to docs/sdk/abort-and-retry-guidance.md and set FailFast as an opt-in preset only; default remains Conservative for backwards compatibility.
Jonas Müller: In the TS implementation the AbortableStream still leaves a socket in some edge cases. I left an inline suggestion to close the reader on error path.
Maya Chen (author): Fixed TS reader close in the follow-up commit. Added a unit test that injects a flaky ReadableStream and asserts resources are released.
Liam O'Connor: Can we ensure the Go API follows Go idioms (context cancel semantics)? I left a suggestion to accept ctx on AbortStream and to return a typed error constant.
Maya Chen (author): Updated Go signature to AbortStream(ctx) and introduced ErrStreamAborted constant; added doc comment with migration note.
ci_summary: Initial CI run: lint failures in ts (missing reader.close on abort), flaky integration test triggered on go race detector; fixes pushed. Subsequent run: all checks green (unit, integration, linters).
validation: Manual verification: ran integration harness against hosted staging and local dedicated env. Verified that abort signals produce ErrStreamAborted/AbortError shapes in their respective SDKs and that FailFast profile limits retries to 2 attempts and transitions to short backoff before circuit-open logging. Added telemetry events for "sdk.retry.circuit_open" and "sdk.stream.abort.requested"; confirmed events appear in staging metrics.
upgrade_notes: This change is opt-in for most users: FailFast presets are not the default. To opt in: set retry_profile='failfast' in client options or use the FailFastRetryPolicy factory in Go. Stream abort APIs are additive: StreamHandle.abort() (py/ts) or AbortStream(ctx) (go) are available immediately. See docs/sdk/abort-and-retry-guidance.md for migration examples.
release_notes:
- Add fail-fast retry profiles (opt-in) to improve latency behavior for interactive apps.
- Add explicit stream abort APIs to Python (StreamHandle.abort), TypeScript (AbortableStream.abort), and Go (AbortStream(ctx)) to allow deterministic cancellation with a uniform error shape.
- SDK bumps: python 2.5.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 1.7.2.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: customers might enable FailFast without understanding throughput tradeoffs. Mitigation: opt-in by default and clear decision table in docs; added telemetry to detect misuse. Risk: abort semantics could leak resources on older runtimes. Mitigation: added unit + integration tests and backfilled reader close paths in TS and finalizers in Python.
notes: Marked as a coordinated SDK release. Changelog updated and release artifacts staged. Post-merge: schedule a follow-up patch to expose a higher-level 'circuit inspector' telemetry view in Console.
